title: Transcribe the pinned benchmark claim permit-list into a production refusal surface
description:
PREREQUISITE for task-09008b4c (GA activation record), filed by architect-ac8532da on 2026-08-27 at HEAD e53b8b81 under the global rail's clause 2: an acceptance row whose certified capability is absent must produce prerequisite PRODUCTION rows with the gap measured symbol by symbol, never a narrowed DoD. architect-474a0c03 measured this gap on 2026-08-23 and it is unchanged today.

THE GAP, measured: `git grep -rn "permit-list\|permitList\|PERMIT_LIST" HEAD -- apps packages scripts tools tests` returns exactly ONE hit and it is a doc comment inside a test (packages/benchmark/campaigns/task-3a34adca.../freeze-record.test.ts:72). There is NO production artifact carrying the claim ladder, no rung resolver, and nothing that can refuse an unpermitted sentence. task-09008b4c DoD 1 ("PASS or explicitly non-applicable by the permit list") and DoD 4 ("the release record permits only scoped claims supported by the exact evidence") are therefore graded against a surface that does not exist.

THE SOURCE IS PINNED AND READABLE — verified this session, not assumed: `sha256sum "D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-best-tool-benchmark-spec.md"` = a62b90436cc0b911fb28526af7b7e0f2d1370f6f93db91c26077f6e2956a589c, byte-identical to the SHA pinned in this epic's rail 1 and in task-09008b4c's rail 1 (101588 bytes). Section 1 "The claim ladder" (:79-91) is the authority: five rungs L1..L5 with gate ids G-L1..G-L5; "Grammar is permit-list, not forbid-list: each rung enumerates the ONLY sentence templates it licenses (each with mandatory scope); any sentence not affirmatively permitted at the reached rung is forbidden, at every rung, including synonyms"; "A rung prints PASS only when every gate at it and below is PASS; any UNKNOWN gate forces the rung UNKNOWN; any FAIL gate forces the rung FAIL"; the release report prints the highest all-PASS rung (or L0/none) and the single permitted sentence. Line :91 carries the PERMANENTLY FORBIDDEN set at every rung including L5 — unscoped/undated superlatives; "best" lacking the four-part scope (date, corpus, target user, named cohort); "production-ready for all users"; the two-sided equivalence words "equals"/"matching"/"on par"/"parity"/"same as"; "cheaper"/"lower cost"; any number not linked to raw evidence; any exact ratio across incompatible price bases.

NOT IN SCOPE: running the benchmark, computing any gate verdict, editing the pinned spec (epic rail 1), or issuing any claim. This row builds the REFUSAL SURFACE only: transcription + resolver + tests. It is not human-gated — the spec is a pinned, readable, SHA-verified document, so transcribing it is engineering, not a product decision.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first: re-`sha256sum` the pinned spec and require a62b90436cc0b911fb28526af7b7e0f2d1370f6f93db91c26077f6e2956a589c (a drifted source is a block, never a transcription from memory); re-run the permit-list grep and require the gap still open (else the surface exists — duplicate, report blocked); record both outputs in a row comment.

A production module carries the claim ladder as an IMMUTABLE frozen roster — one entry per rung {rungId L1..L5, gateId G-L1..G-L5, the permitted sentence TEMPLATE verbatim, its mandatory scope slots} — plus the permanently-forbidden set from spec :91 as its own frozen roster, and pins the spec SHA as a constant beside them so a future spec edit is detectable.

A production resolver takes a per-gate verdict map and answers the highest all-PASS rung or L0/none, applying the spec's own rule: any UNKNOWN forces the rung UNKNOWN, any FAIL forces FAIL, and a rung passes only when every gate at it AND BELOW passes; an unknown or absent gate id is refused with a stable code at the module's layer rather than treated as PASS.

A production refusal surface answers `permitted(sentence, reachedRung)`: a sentence that is not affirmatively one of the reached rung's templates is REFUSED with an exact stable code and the module's layer, and every member of the forbidden roster is refused at EVERY rung including L5 — including the synonym cases the spec names ("safest", "more reliable", "higher quality", "production-ready", "parity", "cheaper").

Roster denominators pinned in their own numbered plan step (epic rail 7): the rung roster asserts an EXACT count of 5 and the forbidden roster an EXACT nonzero count, both as named immutable constants, each drilled by deleting one member and proving the named count assertion reds with nonzero execution.

Focused suite runs standalone with nonzero `Test Files`/`Tests` counts and `pnpm --filter <owning package> typecheck` exits 0; mutation drills red a NAMED arm each: downgrade an UNKNOWN gate to PASS → the rung arm reds; delete one forbidden phrase → its refusal arm reds; loosen the template match to a substring → the unpermitted-sentence arm reds. Every production file ≤ 250 target / 400 bound; explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-09008b4cb39c4a15aa661540d20e9b9b as the consumer.
taskRails: Transcribe the pinned spec verbatim; never paraphrase a template, never invent a rung, never soften the forbidden set. The spec is read-only (epic rail 1).
UNKNOWN is never PASS and an absent gate is never PASS — fail closed with a stable code and layer.
This row issues no claim, runs no benchmark and computes no gate verdict; it only makes an unpermitted claim unsayable.
TDD, exact refusal code and layer, per-file size caps, explicit-pathspec commits.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Put the ladder in packages/contracts — rejected: the pinned benchmark spec's vocabulary already lives in packages/benchmark (campaign records, projection vocabulary), and contracts carries runtime command/query vocabulary, a different axis. (2) One module — rejected: transcription, rung resolution and sentence permitting are three responsibilities and one file would crowd the 250 target; three modules at ~150 lines each with their `.js` bridges match the package's own convention. (3) Derive the rungs programmatically from the spec at runtime — rejected: the spec lives OUTSIDE the repo (D:/projexts/moes/...), so a runtime read would make production depend on an unversioned path; the transcription is committed and the SHA is asserted instead. (4) Substring matching for permitted sentences — rejected and drilled against: the spec's grammar is permit-list, so an appended unsupported clause must refuse. (5) Export the layer constant — rejected: a column-zero `export const *_LAYER` becomes a scanned security boundary owing hostile arms (the exact cost task-d1145412 is paying); type-only export keeps it private.
